The GL double-layered cloak consists of two sphere annular layers: the inner layer has a radius between R1 and R2, and the outer layer has a radius between R2 and R3.
The outer layer cloak of the GL double-layered cloak has the invisibility function, while the inner layer cloak has full absorption function.

When the source is located outside of the GL double-layered cloak, the excited electromagnetic wave field propagation outside of the double layered cloak is the same as in free space and never disturbed by the cloak.

When local sources are located inside the GL double-layered cloak's concealment with normal electromagnetic materials, the excited wave is completely absorbed by the inner layer cloak and never propagates outside of the inner layer.

The GL double-layered cloak overcomes the drawbacks and difficulties of single-layer cloaks and avoids the disputing on the electromagnetic phenomenon inside the single-layered cloaked concealment with normal materials.

The authors prove theoretically and through 3D GL simulations that there exists no Maxwell electromagnetic wave field that can be excited by nonzero local sources inside the single-layered cloaked concealment with normal materials.
The GL method used in this paper is fast, accurate, and can handle dispersive materials without suffering from numerical dispersion issues like finite element and finite difference methods.

The GL double-layered cloak is composed of an anisotropic material in the inner layer and a different anisotropic material in the outer layer, which are coupled at the interface boundary between the two layers.

The simulations show that when the source is outside the cloak, the excited wave propagates the same as in free space and is never disturbed by the cloak, and when the source is inside the concealment, the wave is completely absorbed by the inner layer and never reaches outside the cloak.
The GL method does not require artificial boundaries or PML conditions, which are needed in conventional numerical methods like finite element and finite difference.
The GL double-layered metamaterials are weak degenerative and weak dispersive.

The GL method is a significant scattering process which reduces the numerical dispersion and is suitable to simulate physical wave field scattering in the materials, in particular, for dispersive materials.

The GL method divides the domain as a set of small sub domains or sub lattices, and the Global field is updated by the local field from the interaction between the global field and local subdomain materials successively.
The GL method can be meshless, including arbitrary geometry subdomains, such as rectangle, cylindrical and spherical coordinate mixed coupled together, and it is a full parallel algorithm.
The GL method does not need to solve large matrix equation, it only needs to solve 3x3 and 6x6 matrix equations.
